response: Yes, student examiners can be a reasonable substitute for faculty in an undergraduate OSCE (Objective Structured Clinical Examination) on medical emergencies, provided they are well-trained and calibrated to assess student performance accurately. Research has shown that student examiners can be reliable and valid assessors of clinical skills, particularly when they are given clear guidelines and criteria to evaluate student performance. Additionally, using student examiners can also provide them with valuable experience and skills in assessment and evaluation, which can be beneficial for their own professional development. However, it's essential to ensure that student examiners are properly trained, supervised, and monitored to maintain the integrity and validity of the assessment process.
